think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 50-year-old woman presents with a 1-year history of a hard, irregular left breast mass with skin puckering and nipple retraction, alongside ipsilateral axillary lymphadenopathy. Cytology confirms infiltrating ductal carcinoma with malignant nodal deposits. The unexpected tension is that surgical clearance of the axilla unmasks florid tuberculous lymphadenitis coexisting with metastatic deposits in the same nodal basin in an asymptomatic patient without pulmonary disease.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission presentation concludes with clinical examination of the breast and axilla, complete hemogram showing mild anemia, normal ESR, normal chest radiograph, and normal abdominal ultrasound. Invasive needle cytology, surgical mastectomy, and histopathology represent the confirmatory stage.
3. Differential Distinctions: Pure metastatic adenocarcinoma of the breast was the prevailing diagnosis given the primary tumor, but histopathology showed that nodal enlargement was predominantly driven by caseating granulomatous inflammation. Non-specific reactive hyperplasia was excluded by the presence of true necrotizing granulomas and acid-fast bacilli.
case_prompt: A 50-year-old woman presented with a 1-year history of a painless, slowly enlarging lump in her left breast. She had no family history of breast malignancy, no prior use of oral contraceptives or estrogen therapy, and no history of nipple discharge. General physical examination was unremarkable. Local examination of the left breast revealed a 6.0 x 3.0 cm, hard, irregular, non-tender, mobile lump involving mainly the lower outer quadrant, with puckering of the overlying skin and nipple retraction. Two slightly tender lymph nodes were palpable in the ipsilateral left axilla. The contralateral breast and axilla were normal. Routine preoperative baseline workup showed mild microcytic hypochromic anemia on complete hemogram, while erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), plain chest radiography, and abdominal ultrasound were within normal limits.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Isolated metastatic ductal carcinoma (without concurrent infectious lymphadenitis)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The breast mass and palpable axillary lymphadenopathy were clinically and cytologically diagnosed as carcinoma metastatic to axillary lymph nodes; however, final histopathology demonstrated that nodal enlargement was overwhelmingly due to coexistent granulomatous inflammation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The patient was referred for fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) with the clinical diagnosis of carcinoma of the left breast with axillary lymph nodes involvement... Diagnosis offered on cytology was ductal carcinoma of the left breast with metastasis to the left axillary lymph nodes.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Tender axillary lymphadenopathy adjacent to a breast neoplasm could represent reactive hyperplasia, but histopathology revealed necrotizing caseating granulomas rather than benign reactive proliferation alone.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: two of the lymph nodes showed coexistent carcinomatous deposits along with well defined caseating granulomas and reactive hyperplasia in one.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Histopathological examination of 14 excised axillary lymph nodes revealed that 13 nodes harbored tuberculous lymphadenitis with caseating granulomas and Langhans' giant cells, confirmed by a positive Ziehl-Neelsen stain for acid-fast bacilli coexisting with carcinomatous deposits.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Of the fourteen lymph nodes, thirteen showed tuberculous lymphadenitis in the form of numerous well formed caseating granulomas composed of epithelioid cells, Langhans' giant cells surrounded by lymphocytes, two of the lymph nodes showed coexistent carcinomatous deposits along with well defined caseating granulomas and reactive hyperplasia in one. Ziehl Neelsen stain for acid- fast bacilli was positive (Figure 1, Figure 2)

editor_comments: Admission narrative strictly maintained prior to FNAC cytology, surgery, and histopathology. Zero pathogen names in presentation. Verbatim quotes matched.
